provenance_note: Statuses reached via adoption carry provenance tags; plain VERIFIED means pin identity/design-only as before. Adjudication method: LLM_ADJUDICATION; tier per record as recorded in adoption_records.json (RATIFIED_HUMAN records are human-ratified; others remain ADOPTED_LLM_PROVISIONAL pending human ratification).

adoption_records.decision: RECOVERY_AUTHORITY = wal_triad_bridge fail-closed IN_DOUBT retention; wal.lisp start-of-recovery ABORT resolution is a violation pending repair
adoption_records.adopted_rule: PREPARED transactions are never resolved by assumption at recovery start. Unresolved transactions stay IN_DOUBT — isolated, never canonical, never in the replay set — until an explicit resolution frame (COMMITTED or ABORTED) arrives.

adoption_records.decision: WAL_TAIL_POLICY = quarantine (preserve partial tail records, exclude from canonical replay); truncation forbidden without an explicitly adopted norm plus recorded evidence
adoption_records.adopted_rule: Incomplete records at recovery are quarantined, never truncated. Truncation requires an explicitly adopted storage norm and recorded evidence; the existing truncation behaviour is a violation pending repair.

adoption_records.decision: DURABILITY_NORM = fdatasync success of a fully written record as the local linearization point; Canonical-History precedence restricted to local scope until a join path exists
adoption_records.adopted_rule: Durability = successful fdatasync of a fully written record (append-and-sync). Precedence against Canonical History is not adopted: transaction-index claims hold in local scope only until a Canonical-History comparison path exists.

adoption_records.decision: PRECEDENCE RULE = wal_triad_bridge is canonical authority for transaction/state semantics; runtime/phase-d/wal.lisp is a legacy physical WAL surface, non-authoritative for canonical state until aligned with ADR-001/ADR-002
adoption_records.adopted_rule: When implementation surfaces diverge on the same state semantics, the fail-closed bridge is authoritative. The wal.lisp recovery path is legacy and non-authoritative until repaired to the adopted norms.

adoption_records.decision: CONVENTION = full-chapter span (ledger pin ranges) is the unit of chapter identity going forward; pre-regen records stay labelled as covering pre-regen ranges
adoption_records.adopted_rule: Chapter identity is the ledger pin range (full-chapter span), not an interior-H1 split. Records written under the pre-regen segmentation are labelled as covering pre-regen ranges; they are not rewritten.

adoption_records.decision: SCOPE = pass stays scoped to the freeze-pinned 127-unit corpus; the 99 unpinned chapters (125-149.md, 150-174.md, 175-199.md, 200-218.md) are excluded until pinned and freeze-recorded
adoption_records.adopted_rule: The implementation-verification pass covers exactly the CORPUS-FREEZE-MDSHEETS-01 chapter files (127 units). Unpinned chapters may enter only after pinning and a recorded freeze; extending the pass without a freeze is not authorized.

adoption_records.decision: INDEX = adopt the regenerated chapters_index.md (live digest 595a41b66c...) as the index record; chron_os_architecture_summary.md excluded as a non-chapter sheet; re-record requires human ratification
adoption_records.adopted_rule: chapters_index.md carries the live regen digest; the recorded pre-regen digest is superseded with provenance. Index re-recording is provisional until human ratification; the freeze manifest for chapter files is untouched.

adoption_records.decision: CONVENTION = LF-only line convention adopted; the three recorded anchor-line digest mismatches (mdsu0000, mdsu0014, mdsu0016) stay reported as observed, not corrected in the immutable layer
adoption_records.adopted_rule: Anchor-line digests are computed under the LF-only corpus convention without a trailing-newline convention. Existing mismatched stored digests remain as recorded evidence of the old convention; re-recording pending ratification.

applied_effects.reason: CON-INV-07 adopted as governing recovery norm; bridge satisfies it; wal.lisp recorded as violation pending repair
anti-truncation norm adopted as governing tail policy; code#02 truncation and the test assertion recorded as violations pending repair
linearization point = durability confirmation adopted; code#01 semantic join holds under the adopted norm
txid duplicate detection holds locally under adopted durability norm; Canonical-History precedence half stays unresolved pending join path
WAL state-semantics claim classified under adopted authority; evidence remains keyword-level, so scope is restricted, not verified

conflict_matrix_entries.why: code resolves PREPARED to ABORT at recovery start with no confirmation step — assumption is the operation itself
claim forbids truncation without an explicit storage norm and evidence; code truncates on recovery start with no such precondition
test asserts exactly the behaviour the claim forbids; test and design norm cannot both hold

structural: precedence semantics require a comparison path with Canonical History; no Canonical History surface exists in the code corpus, so the requirement cannot be satisfied — code resolves status from its local tx table alone
recovery-evidence precedence is undecided in the design; two surfaces encode opposite rules (wal.lisp resolves at start, bridge is fail-closed)
